title: HTTP-Cookies
info: HTTP-Cookies are a technology designed to help users online. Due to the internets capabilities the need to collect some user data is completely necessary for a smooth user experience. This is for example keeping the products in a shopping cart, going through different sites, while online shopping. In recent years these cookies have been more advanced, and digital services allows for more cookies to be used. Now instead of just keeping the content of your online shopping cart, you also have cookies containing your user data. This could be your gender, interests, religion, sexuality etc.
code: Be aware of what kind of data you collect
Understand what data you need to collect
Do not collect data that is not necessary for your business

title: Sharing data
info: Selling cookies is quite normal. Sometimes it is necessary for delivering a good product. The problem here is that it can be hard finding out where the data is ending up. An example of this is Spotify. They share user data with 92+ vendors. Some of these again share the data further. To for example Quantcast, a company made for selling user data
code: Don’t share the data if you don’t know where it ends up.
Be aware of who your business share data with
Be aware of how business partners share data
Take responsibility if you are to lose sensitive user information

title: Using data
info: If your business is buying user data to use, you should also be aware of the effects this may have. Both social medias, internet-browsers, news outlets and other websites use this data in ways that are not necessarily transparent to the user. This is often seen through algorithmic feeds and targeted advertisements. In social media the algorithmic feeds may lead to extremism, depression or lack of concentration. If your business is working in this area, you should have a look at the impact you make on your users and take action to reduce such risks.
code: Use the data in a way that is in the interest of the user
Do not analyse user data to a point where you end up knowing more about the user than they do themselves
Do not use what you know about the user to nudge user attitudes and values

title: Informing users
info: When collecting user data, you should let them know you are doing it. This will allow the user to know what is collected from them. This is stated through the EU’s General Data Protection Regulation. If you are collecting user data it is important to have a well written, and easily understood, consent declaration.
code: Everything you use of users personal data should be visible and transparent to the user.
Use simple language informing users about how you use their data.
Let it be easy to find the relevant information for the user.
Don’t add more information than what is necessary to the user.
Be aware of the difficulty it is to read the consent document.

title: User consent
info: Online we can see that you always must accept or reject the use of cookies. This is the consent users give to businesses. Consent is also not straight forward. Consent should be voluntarily, and fair. The user should be able to not consent to the use of their data, and also do it on their own terms. Some typical consents we see today goes against this. Here we see dark patterns, or the business-model: Pay or Okay.Dark patterns are design choices which guides the user to consenting without even thinking about what they are consenting to. It should be just as easy to consent as not.
code: Users should have a saying in the use of their data
Denying sharing of data should be just as easy as consenting to it

title: Pay or Okay
info: Pay or okay is a new business-model. It was made popular by Meta. This business model states that you are to consent to the usage, and selling of your data. If you don’t want this, you could pay for them not to sell it. This is not a valid consent. This also make privacy a luxury good, which you must pay for.
code: Avoid using procedures which jeopardises users consent
If the options are between paying with money or user data, you should add another option
